prf:level-sufficiency:
Proof Proof of level sufficiency. The Ocneanu–Jones Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M: H_\bullet(q) \to \mathbb{C}(q) is a compatible family along the Hecke tower H_n(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n+1}(R, q). It satisfies the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M \circ \iota = \mathrm{tr}_M (Jones 1987). Hypothesis k_{\max}(P, q) \le n_0 asserts that every Wedderburn block \lambda \vdash k with k > n_0 has zero projection in T_w^{\downarrow}. Under the inclusion \iota: H_{n_0}(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n_1}(R, q) this vanishing is preserved. The additional blocks \lambda \vdash k with n_0 < k \le n_1 accessible at the fine level contribute zero to T_w^{\uparrow} = \iota\,T_w^{\downarrow}. Thus \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\uparrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\iota\,T_w^{\downarrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\downarrow}) by the Markov property. Functoriality of \mathrm{tr}_M: \mathbf{Conf} \to \mathbb{C}(q) (confinement category) extends this equality to every composite of unfoldings, establishing preservation along the full confinement chain.

For a general trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} that factors through \mathrm{tr}_M, equality of traces implies equality of values: \mathcal{F}(P^{\uparrow}) = \mathcal{F}(P). \square

Converse (unfolding necessity). If k_{\max}(P, q) > n_0 — the witnessed partition content of P exceeds the coarse strand count — then no representation of T_w^{\downarrow} as an element of H_{n_0}(q) captures all tight dual blocks of the confinement SDP. Unfolding to the smallest level n_1 with k_{\max}(P, q, n_1) \le n_1 is strictly required. The unfolded trace \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\uparrow}) differs from any coarse surrogate by contributions from the additional blocks. Magic shell closure and multi-operator binding configurations (\mu(S, q) \ge 2) are the principal triggers.

Corollary (default-coarse computability). Every trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} computed at the coarsest level satisfying k_{\max} \le n is exact. Default-coarse computation is not a performance heuristic. It is the content of this proposition.
rem:level-sufficiency-interprets:
Remark Physical interpretation of level sufficiency: default coarse, unfold on witness. This proposition is the formal justification for a default-coarse computational strategy across the full confinement category. The hierarchy has at least four relevant levels:

Level \ell Confined particle Default strand count n_0
0 quark 1
1 nucleon (proton, neutron) 3 (quark-strands)
2 atom / nucleus A (nucleon-strands)
3 compound / molecule # atoms

At each level, any trace-class invariant is exact at the coarsest representation satisfying k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) \le n_0.

Default-coarse rule. Every computational pipeline executes the following steps:

  1. Identify the confined particle P at its natural level \ell.
  2. Read k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) from the witness data.
  3. If k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) \le n_0, compute \mathrm{tr}_M at the coarse level and halt.
  4. If k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) > n_0, apply the unfolding morphism \uparrow_\ell and repeat at \ell - 1.

Unfolding triggers.

  • Magic shell closure. Atoms at A \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} and noble-gas electron counts Z \in \{2, 10, 18, 36, 54, 86\} exhibit binding multiplicity \mu(S, q) \ge 2. This forces k_{\max} above the coarse count. Atoms in these rows evaluate one level deeper.
  • SDP cross-channel demand. The active dual support \mathcal{S}^* of the confinement SDP spans blocks \lambda_1, \lambda_2. When \max(|\lambda_1|, |\lambda_2|) > n_0, the coarse representation cannot express the coupling. Unfolding is required.

Non-magic atoms and molecules without SDP cross-channel demand evaluate at their natural coarse level. This is the minimal exact representation.

Dressing preserves computational minimality. Under the dressing morphism \mathrm{dress}_S: P_{\mathrm{bare}} \to P_{\mathrm{dressed}}, the witnessed truncation updates to

  k_{\max}(P_{\mathrm{dressed}}, q)
  \;=\;
  \max\bigl(k_{\max}(P_{\mathrm{bare}}, q),\;
            k_{\max}^{\mathrm{bind}}(S, q)\bigr),

where k_{\max}^{\mathrm{bind}} is the partition reach of the binding subword W_{\mathrm{bind}}. The dressed particle's computational level follows from the updated k_{\max}. Adding a single electron to a non-magic atom typically leaves the computational level unchanged. Closing to a noble gas triggers \mu \ge 2 and raises the required level.

Computational implication. For a non-magic atom with A nucleons, the Hecke algebra dimension drops from |H_{3A}(q)| = (3A)! to |H_A(R, q)| = A!. Partition enumeration drops from p(3A) to p(A). Default-coarse computation is the computational content of this proposition applied via the confinement category.
prop:confinement-phase-stratification:
Proposition The confinement locus is open, and the active support is constant on a strictly complementary phase. Let P be a confined particle, and let the substrate parameter q range over \mathbb{R}_{>1}. Write strict feasibility of the confinement SDP as a finite system of strict inequalities 0 < g_i(q, X), i \in I, in q and the decision variable X, with each g_i continuous. (Positive definiteness of a Gram matrix is such a system, by Sylvester's criterion on its leading principal minors.) The confinement locus of P is

  \Omega(P) \;:=\; \{\, q : \exists X,\ \forall i \in I,\ 0 < g_i(q, X) \,\}.

Let u^*_\lambda(q) be the dual variables of the SDP and s_\lambda(q) the matching primal slacks. The active support is \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) := \{\lambda : u^*_\lambda(q) > 0\} and the binding multiplicity is \mu(P, q) := |\mathcal{S}^*(P, q)|. Then:

  1. Openness. \Omega(P) is open.
  2. Constancy on a phase. Let C \subseteq \Omega(P) be connected. Suppose u^*_\lambda and s_\lambda are continuous in q, complementary (u^*_\lambda s_\lambda = 0) and strictly complementary (u^*_\lambda > 0 or s_\lambda > 0) at every q \in C. Then \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) and \mu(P, q) are constant on C.

The remaining structure of the phases (the boundary stratification, analyticity of the Frobenius stability index, scope and phase transitions) is stated separately in the phase-boundary conjecture below.

Archimedean specialisation. Both parts sit on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: the locus is a subset of \mathbb{R}, and openness and connectedness are statements about the real topology.
prf:confinement-phase-stratification:
Proof Proof of confinement phase stratification. Claim (1)—Openness. Let S := \{(q, X) : \forall i,\ 0 < g_i(q, X)\}. Each set \{0 < g_i\} is open because g_i is continuous, and I is finite, so S is open. \Omega(P) is the image of S under the projection (q, X) \mapsto q, which is an open map. Hence \Omega(P) is open.

Claim (2)—Constancy on a phase. Fix \lambda. Let U := \{q : u^*_\lambda(q) > 0\} and V := \{q : s_\lambda(q) > 0\}; both are open by continuity. Strict complementarity gives C \subseteq U \cup V. If C met both U and V, then, C being connected, it would meet U \cap V at some q; there u^*_\lambda(q)\, s_\lambda(q) > 0, contradicting complementarity. So either u^*_\lambda > 0 on all of C, or u^*_\lambda > 0 nowhere on C. This holds for every \lambda, so \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) is the same set for every q \in C, and so is its size \mu(P, q). \square
rem:confinement-phase-stratification-int: Remark Topology of the confinement locus \Omega(P). For simple particles, \Omega(P) is expected to be a single connected interval of \mathbb{R}_{>1} containing q_0; neither connectedness nor q_0 \in \Omega(P) is proved. For composite particles with multi-block binding, \Omega(P) can be disconnected. Each component corresponds to a distinct configuration of the active support. One physically realises transitions between components as chemical or nuclear rearrangements. Computationally, they appear as regime switches in the witness files.
conj:confinement-phase-boundaries:
Conjecture Phase boundaries of the confinement locus. Let P be a confined particle, with confinement locus \Omega(P), active support \mathcal{S}^*(P, q), binding multiplicity \mu(P, q) and Frobenius stability index \sigma_F(P, q) as in prop:confinement-phase-stratification. Let \mathcal{G} \subset \mathbb{R}_{>1} be the generic locus of q, and call a connected component \Omega_\alpha of \Omega(P) a confinement phase. Then:

  1. Stratification. The complement \mathcal{G} \setminus \Omega(P) is a real-algebraic stratification with strata of codimension \ge 1, the phase boundaries of P. Each stratum is the zero locus of a principal minor of the SDP Gram matrix.
  2. Strict complementarity on phases. On each phase \Omega_\alpha the SDP dual pair is continuous and strictly complementary, so the active support and \mu are constant on \Omega_\alpha by prop:confinement-phase-stratification.
  3. Analyticity. \sigma_F(P, q) is real-analytic on each \Omega_\alpha.
  4. Scope. Level sufficiency, shell-closure stability and the Markov-trace preservation of the confinement category functor hold pointwise in each \Omega_\alpha and fail on \partial\Omega(P).
  5. Phase transitions. If a continuous path q: [0, 1] \to \mathcal{G} crosses a phase boundary at q_0 \in \partial\Omega(P), then at q_0 either P is not realisable as a closed-braid bound state (deconfinement), or \mu jumps, the active support gains or loses a Wedderburn block, and \sigma_F has a non-smooth point (regime switch), or both.

Supporting argument (not a proof). For (1): the entries of the Gram matrix are Laurent polynomials in q, so each principal minor that is not identically zero has finitely many real zeros in \mathcal{G}; what is not shown is that loss of strict feasibility happens exactly on these zero sets. For (2): strict complementarity holds for generic SDP data (Alizadeh–Haeberly–Overton), but genericity at the substrate parameters is not established. For (4): the proofs of prop:level-sufficiency and prop:shell-closure-stability use a well-defined, locally constant active support. For (5): a boundary crossing is either a loss of strict primal feasibility or a dual variable u^*_\lambda passing through zero.
rem:phase-scoped-applicability:
Remark Phase-scoped applicability: confinement theorems hold on open strata only. The phase-boundary conjecture (conj:confinement-phase-boundaries) proposes the scope caveat attached to every statement in the confinement framework. Any formal statement about a confined particle P, its electron shell, a dressing morphism, or a trace-class invariant \mathcal{F}(P) includes the implicit quantifier:

  \forall\, q \in \Omega_\alpha(P),

where \Omega_\alpha(P) is a fixed connected component of the confinement locus \Omega(P), a single confinement phase.

Conjecturally phase-scoped results (conjectured to hold only within a single \Omega_\alpha):

  • Level sufficiency: preservation of Markov trace under unfolding.
  • Shell-closure stability: monotonicity of \sigma_F along the dressing chain and local maxima at noble-gas Z.
  • Functoriality of \mathrm{tr}_M: \mathbf{Conf} \to \mathbb{C}(q).
  • Multi-operator binding structure: constancy of the active support.

Boundary phenomena (not covered by the phase-scoped results):

  • Deconfinement events. At q \in \partial\Omega(P) with Slater-strict feasibility lost, P ceases to be realisable as a closed-braid bound state.
  • Regime switches. At q \in \partial\Omega(P) with a \mu-jump but preserved feasibility, the active support gains or loses a Wedderburn block.
  • Critical scaling. Near a phase boundary, \sigma_F typically has a non-analytic limit.
  • Chemical and nuclear rearrangements. Transitions between disconnected components of \Omega(P) for a composite P are realised physically as structural rearrangements. These transitions require an explicit cross-component analysis using the stratification of \Omega(P).

Practical reading. When encountering a confinement-framework statement, treat q as ranging over a fixed open phase unless the text addresses boundary behaviour. Numerical witnesses evaluate at a single q = q_0 \approx 1.110. As long as that point lies in \Omega_\alpha(P), the phase-scoped results apply wherever they hold. Auditing behaviour across q ranges requires explicit stratification analysis.
def:lp-stable: Definition LP-stable element of H_3(q). An element x \in H_3(q) with NF decomposition x = \sum_{i=1}^{6} x_i b_i is LP-stable if Gx \geq 0 (component-wise), where G is the Gram matrix G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j).
def:lp-confined: Definition LP-confined element of H_3(q). An element x \in H_3(q) is LP-confined if x is LP-stable and no proper sub-braid is LP-stable.
prop:nuclear-chamber-groebner-basis:
Proposition Physical cluster chamber, drip-line monomer reduction, and the Hoyle triple-alpha bottleneck. Let R be a linearly ordered additive commutative group, and consider the 1s-shell motif conservation matrix

  A_0 \;=\; \begin{pmatrix}
    1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\
    0 & 1 & 1 & 2 & 1 & 2
  \end{pmatrix} \in \mathbb{Z}^{2 \times 6}

indexing the commutative polynomial generators (x_p, x_n, x_d, x_t, x_h, x_\alpha) of proton, neutron, deuteron, triton, helion, and \alpha-particle counts under conservation of (Z, N). Let I_{A_0} = \langle x^{g^+} - x^{g^-} : A_0 g = 0 \rangle denote the associated toric ideal [conti-traverso1991, sturmfels-thomas1997], and write c = (0, 0, -B_d, -B_t, -B_h, -B_\alpha) \in R^6 for the cluster cost vector reduced modulo the row span of A_0.

  1. Graver and Gröbner fan structure. Over \mathbb{Q}, the integer kernel \ker_{\mathbb{Z}}(A_0) admits 28 unsigned primitive Graver binomials [graver1975] (17 unsigned circuits), a 27-element unsigned universal Gröbner basis (excluding only x_\alpha - x_p x_n x_d), and 73 full-dimensional Gröbner fan chambers in R^6 / \mathrm{row}(A_0) \cong R^4.

  2. Physical chamber \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{phys}} and 11-rule reduced Gröbner basis. Whenever (B_d, B_t, B_h, B_\alpha) \in R^4 satisfies the five irredundant facet inequalities

  0 < B_d, \qquad
  B_d < B_h, \qquad
  B_d < B_t, \qquad
  2 B_t < B_\alpha, \qquad
  2 B_h < B_\alpha,

all eleven binomials of the minimal reduced Gröbner basis \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{phys}} are simultaneously strictly cost-decreasing (c \cdot g > 0):

  \begin{aligned}
    x_p x_n &\to x_d, &
    x_p x_d &\to x_h, &
    x_n x_d &\to x_t, &
    x_p x_t &\to x_\alpha, \\
    x_n x_h &\to x_\alpha, &
    x_d^2 &\to x_\alpha, &
    x_d x_t &\to x_n x_\alpha, &
    x_d x_h &\to x_p x_\alpha, \\
    x_t x_h &\to x_d x_\alpha, &
    x_t^2 &\to x_n^2 x_\alpha, &
    x_h^2 &\to x_p^2 x_\alpha . &
  \end{aligned}

Both the bare and tower-resummed substrate binding energies at q_0 lie strictly inside \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{phys}}.

  1. Drip-line dissociation and integer parity monomers. Reduction modulo \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{phys}} carries {}^5\mathrm{He} (x_p^2 x_n^3) deterministically to the irreducible degree-2 disconnected normal form x_\alpha x_n, while mapping {}^{12}\mathrm{C} (x_p^6 x_n^6 \mapsto x_\alpha^3), {}^{14}\mathrm{N} (x_p^7 x_n^7 \mapsto x_d x_\alpha^3), {}^9\mathrm{Be} (x_p^4 x_n^5 \mapsto x_n x_\alpha^2), and {}^9\mathrm{B} (x_p^5 x_n^4 \mapsto x_p x_\alpha^2) to integer cluster normal forms without fractional continuous-relaxation artifacts.

  2. Degree-3 Hoyle bottleneck and capacitated shell confluence. On the (\alpha, {}^8\mathrm{Be}, {}^{12}\mathrm{C}) baryon-number sublattice A_{\mathrm{Hoyle}} = (4, 8, 12), the inequalities 2 c_\alpha < c_{{}^8\mathrm{Be}} and c_{{}^{12}\mathrm{C}} < 3 c_\alpha simultaneously orient the endothermic fission binomial x_{{}^8\mathrm{Be}} \to x_\alpha^2 and the degree-3 fusion binomial x_\alpha^3 \to x_{{}^{12}\mathrm{C}}. Adjoining the seven Mayer--Jensen shell occupation and hole variables u_s + w_s = C_s for C_s \in \{2, 6, 12, 8, 22, 32, 44\} recovers cumulative magic closures (2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126) and guarantees u_s > 0 or w_s > 0 on every physical fiber C_s \ge 1, so the S - 1 adjacent single-shell promotions u_{s+1} w_s \to u_s w_{s+1} are globally confluent.
prf:nuclear-chamber-groebner-basis: Proof Facet implication over ordered groups, finite normal-form confluence, and shell hole positivity.
prop:lp-dual-stability:
Proposition LP dual stability: the confined optimum is LP-stable and strongly dual. Let x^* \in \mathbb{R}^6 be an optimum of the operator-selection linear program

  \min_x \; t^\top x
  \quad\text{subject to}\quad
  \sum_i x_i = n_{\mathrm{target}}, \qquad G x \geq 0, \qquad x \geq 0,

where G is the Frobenius Gram matrix and t is the mass-coefficient vector, so that t^\top x^* = \mathrm{tr}_M(x^*). Then:

  1. x^* is LP-stable: Gx^* \geq 0 in all six channels.
  2. Strong duality holds: there is a dual optimum whose net-constraint shadow price y_0^* satisfies \mathrm{tr}_M(x^*) = y_0^* \cdot n_{\mathrm{target}}.

Both parts hold for every Gram matrix G and cost vector t. Part 1 is the feasibility of x^*, and part 2 is finite-dimensional linear-programming strong duality. The confinement-specific properties of the six-channel matrix at the substrate are recorded in the confinement reading.
rem:lp-dual-stability-confinement-readin:
Remark Confinement reading of the LP-dual stability criterion. Two further properties are claimed for the specific six-channel Gram matrix at the substrate. They are not derived from linear-programming duality, and they are not currently established numerically: the Gram matrix built by the confinement operator-selection computation is singular, so it has no finite condition number, and that computation does not produce shadow prices. They are recorded here rather than in the proposition:

  • The dual shadow prices are bounded by |y_i^*| \leq \kappa(G) \cdot \|t\|, where \kappa(G) is the condition number of G (a value \approx 7.0 was recorded earlier, but the Gram matrix the computation now builds is singular, so this figure is not reproduced). Linear-programming duality alone does not bound shadow prices by the condition number, so the bound would have to come from the matrix itself; for a singular G (\kappa(G) = \infty) it says nothing.
  • The B_3 sub-braid \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} is LP-unstable: G\vec{x} has a negative \sigma_0 component. Partial confinement is therefore not sufficient, and all three units are required.

Individual quarks are LP-stable and the B_3 sub-unit is LP-unstable. In this reading, that is what confinement means algebraically: the gluon field contains an LP-unstable intermediate, and stability returns only for the full 3-fold Borromean product. Stability of the binding operator therefore requires the topologically complete structure; the B_3 sub-unit alone is not enough.

The negative eigenvalue \lambda_{\min} \approx -0.956 (a historical figure; the canonical-weight value is \approx -0.7527, see the Frobenius Gram matrix) gives the LP, without the braid constraint, a global minimum at \mathrm{tr}_M = 0. Requiring the solution to be realised by a braid excludes that minimum.

def:algebraic-primality:
Definition Algebraic primality of a strand count. Fix a substrate parameter q > 1. For each strand count n \geq 1, the confinement SDP selects a canonical state \psi_n(q). Say that n is algebraically prime at q if \psi_n(q) is not contained in the closed span of any non-trivial tensor product

  \overline{\mathrm{span}}\bigl\{\,
    \psi_{n_1}(q) \otimes \cdots \otimes \psi_{n_k}(q)
  \,\bigr\}.

This product is indexed by a decomposition n = n_1 + \cdots + n_k with k \geq 2 and every n_i \geq 1.
rem:algebraic-primality-remark:
Remark Algebraic primality as a magic-number surrogate. By convention, n = 0 is not prime. This predicate serves as a purely algebraic surrogate for a magic strand count. An algebraically prime configuration does not factor into a product of smaller closed configurations.

The definition relies on a recursive decomposition argument. Testing primality at n checks all decompositions into smaller parts. The recursion bottoms out at n = 1. The n=1 state is algebraically prime vacuously, because no decomposition into k \geq 2 positive parts sums to 1.
prop:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic:
Proposition Vacuous primality at n = 1. For every substrate q > 1, the integer n = 1 is algebraically prime. Equivalently, the canonical state \psi_1(q) is not in the closed span of any non-trivial tensor product of canonical states indexed by a decomposition 1 = n_1 + \cdots + n_k with k \geq 2 and n_i \geq 1. No such decomposition exists.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall.
rem:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic-context:
Remark Base case, empirical magic numbers, and archimedean scope of vacuous primality. The proof uses only elementary arithmetic. It uses no SDP analysis, Hecke-algebra machinery, or tensor-product manipulation. This is the base case of the recursion. Every primality check at n \geq 2 ultimately bottoms out at n = 1 through repeated decomposition.

Empirical nuclear magic numbers start at 2. The framework's n = 1 primality is sometimes glossed as below the lowest shell closure. Within the algebraic-primality framework, n = 1 is strictly magic, just for a vacuous reason.

The archimedean specialisation invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic:
Proof Proof of n equals 1 vacuous magic. The claim reduces to a vacuous-truth statement about positive-integer decompositions.

  1. Suppose, for contradiction, that a decomposition 1 = n_1 + n_2 + \cdots + n_k exists with k \geq 2 and n_i \geq 1 for all i = 1, \ldots, k.
  2. Lower-bound the sum: 
      \sum_{i=1}^{k} n_i \;\geq\; \sum_{i=1}^{k} 1 \;=\; k \;\geq\; 2.
  3. By hypothesis \sum_{i=1}^{k} n_i = 1, so 1 \geq 2. Contradiction.
  4. Therefore no decomposition with k \geq 2 and all n_i \geq 1 summing to 1 exists.
  5. The universal-quantifier statement "\psi_1(q) \notin \overline{\mathrm{span}}\{\cdots\} for every such decomposition" ranges over the empty set of decompositions and is vacuously true.

Therefore 1 is algebraically prime at every q > 1. \square
prop:q-beta-cos-resummation:
Proposition \mathfrak{Q}_\beta cos-resummation at z = q^3/(q^2+1): \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\cos} = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{base}} \cdot \cos((z-1)h/2) (conditional on the transfer-matrix eigenphase identification). \mathfrak{Q}_\beta cos-resummation (conditional on the \beta-decay transfer matrix). Let z = q^3/(q^2+1) be the Markov parameter and h = q - q^{-1}. The cos-resummation dresses a \mathfrak{Q}_\beta base by the classical cosine of the half eigenphase:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{cos}}
  \;:=\;
  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{base}} \cdot \cos\alpha,
  \qquad
  \alpha = \tfrac{(z-1)\,h}{2},
  \quad
  z = \tfrac{q^3}{q^2+1},
  \quad
  h = q - q^{-1}.

Since |\cos\alpha| \le 1, the factor is a contraction: it can only lower |\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{base}}|.

The transfer matrix M_\beta is posited to have spectrum \{e^{+i\alpha},\, e^{-i\alpha}\} on the 2-dimensional irreducible representation V_{(2,1)} of H_3(q). Under that identification the Markov trace symmetrizes the two eigenphases:

  \tfrac12\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(M_\beta|_{V_{(2,1)}}\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \cos\alpha
  \;=\;
  \cos\!\bigl(\tfrac{(z-1)\,h}{2}\bigr).

Its numerical evaluation at the proton-anchored q_0 and comparison with CODATA are recorded in the comparison remark.

Non-invariance under the bar involution. Deriving an even resummation factor from q \mapsto q^{-1} would require z(q^{-1}) = z(q) so that \alpha \mapsto -\alpha. For z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1), however, z(q^{-1}) = 1/(q^3+q) \neq z(q) whenever q \neq 1 (unlike bar-symmetric expressions such as 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2})). Consequently, the bar involution does not negate \alpha at z = q^3/(q^2+1), and the cosine factor is stated as a tested definition rather than a consequence of bar symmetry.
rem:q-beta-cos-resummation-comparison:
Remark \mathfrak{Q}_\beta cos-resummation compared with measurement at the proton pin. This remark records the cos-resummation evaluated at the proton-anchored q_0 and compared with the CODATA value.

Comparison with measurement at q_0 \approx 1.1099785827513808. At q_0 one has z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1) \approx 0.6126880371, h \approx 0.2090602988, \alpha = (z-1)h/2 \approx -0.0404857773, and \cos\alpha \approx 0.9991805629. Two bases are recorded side by side; neither is selected by its residual.

  1. Markov-trace \Delta base (\varepsilon evaluated as \mathrm{tr}_M at z = q^3/(q^2+1)), \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\Delta} = \bigl|h^2/2 - h\,z\bigr|\,E_0 with E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)): \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\Delta} \approx 0.4447004085 MeV, residual \approx -431571.9 ppm against CODATA 2022 0.78233355931 MeV. Dressing by \cos\alpha gives \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\Delta,\cos} \approx 0.4443360045 MeV, residual \approx -432037.7 ppm. The cosine factor moves this residual away from zero: the base lies below CODATA, so closing the gap requires a factor exceeding 1, whereas \cos\alpha \le 1 for every real \alpha.
  2. Coordinate-sum Form A (z = 1 comparison), \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^A = m_e\,|q^2-2q-1|(q+1)/(2q^3) \approx 0.7836458274 MeV, residual \approx +1677.4 ppm. Dressed by \cos\alpha at z = q^3/(q^2+1), \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{A,\cos} \approx 0.7830036789 MeV, residual \approx +856.6 ppm (1.96\times smaller).

The scored value applies the T^3 weight split of the z = q^3/(q^2+1) trace to the \gamma\gamma base V^3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3, giving \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx 0.3254 MeV (-58.40\%) (Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay); the \Delta evaluation is retained as an unscored comparison.

sec:nn-isospin-interface-intro:
Four two-nucleon states exist in nature: the three isospin-triplet (T = 1) states (pp, nn, and the symmetric pn configuration), none of which forms a bound state, and the unique isospin-singlet (T = 0) antisymmetric pn state—the deuteron—which binds at 2.224566\;\mathrm{MeV}. A first-principles theory of nuclear interactions must account for both the discrete selection of the T = 0 channel and the numerical value of its binding energy.

Two distinct algebraic mechanisms operate on the two-nucleon braid, and maintaining their separation is essential:

  1. Isospin channel selection: Each two-nucleon isospin channel carries the Wedderburn weight of its symmetry block, \mu_+ for the symmetric triplet and \mu_- for the antisymmetric singlet. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the strict inequality \mu_- < \mu_+ holds identically for all q > 1. Because the logarithmic binding functional B = -\alpha\log\mu is strictly decreasing in \mu, the isospin singlet T = 0 is unconditionally more strongly bound than the triplet T = 1 without parameter tuning.
  2. Interface bond evaluation: In the composite mass pipeline, an inter-nucleon bond contributes a Markov scalar \mu = z + d with deformation parameter d \in [-h, 0], from which the quantitative binding energy is extracted via the same logarithmic functional.

This section proves the universal ordering \mu_- < \mu_+, refutes the naive content-keyed interface alternative, defines the isospin selection map on colour systems, and establishes the branching identity tying the isospin weights to H_n(q). Measuring the admissible interface band [z - h, z] against \mu_- and \mu_+ reveals that the interface interval lies strictly between the two Wedderburn weights (\mu_- < z - h < z < \mu_+), proving that channel selection and bond magnitude operate on disjoint algebraic strata, while the \mathrm{SO}(3) spin fibre and spin–isospin product generate Wigner's \mathrm{SU}(4) supermultiplet symmetry.
prop:isospin-singlet-binds-more:
Proposition \mu_- < \mu_+ for every q>0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1): the isospin singlet is always the more strongly bound channel. Let z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) be the Markov parameter and let

  \mu_+ \;=\; \frac{z + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  \mu_- \;=\; \frac{q - z}{q + q^{-1}}

be the interface scalars of the isospin triplet and singlet. Then

  \boxed{\;\; \mu_- \;<\; \mu_+ \qquad \text{for every } q > 0. \;\;}
prop:content-keyed-interface-refuted:
Proposition No interface keyed on nucleon content can work: the two pn channels share content and differ in boundness. Let \mathrm{content} : \mathrm{Channel} \to \mathrm{Content} send a two-nucleon channel to the unordered pair of nucleon species it contains, and suppose the binding energy factors through it, B = \tilde B \circ \mathrm{content}. Then no such \tilde B reproduces the observed pattern.

The argument needs one input from experiment. The two pn channels have the same content and opposite boundness: pn({}^3S_1) is the deuteron, bound at +2.224566\ \mathrm{MeV}, while pn({}^1S_0) is unbound, a virtual state at -0.066\ \mathrm{MeV}. A function of the content alone assigns them the same value. One channel must therefore be mis-assigned, whatever \tilde B is.
rem:isospin-singlet-binds-more-two-nucle: Remark Which two-nucleon channel the singlet ordering selects. This remark records how the ordering \mu_- < \mu_+ of the isospin interface scalars is read against the measured two-nucleon channels, and the values of the two scalars at q_0.
prf:isospin-singlet-binds-more: Proof Proof: the positive numerator, and the transport to binding energy.
prop:markov-stabilisation-needs-a-fresh-:
Proposition Markov stabilisation at the interface requires a generator the word does not already use. Let \mathbf{A} be a ring carrying a Hecke generator \sigma with \sigma^2 = h\,\sigma + 1, and let \mathrm{tr} be linear with \mathrm{tr}(1) = 1. If \mathrm{tr}(\sigma) = z and Markov stabilisation \mathrm{tr}(W\sigma) = z\,\mathrm{tr}(W) is assumed at W = \sigma, then

  z^2 = h\,z + 1 .

At z = q^3/(q^2+1) with h = q - q^{-1}, that equation has no solution: for every q > 0

  z^2 - h\,z - 1
    \;=\; -\,\frac{(q^2 - q + 1)(q^2 + q + 1)}{(q^2+1)^2}
    \;<\; 0 .

Hence stabilisation fails at a generator the word already uses.

The interface between two nucleons contributes to the Markov trace through a single element a\,\sigma + b\,\mathbf{1} of the two-dimensional subalgebra that \sigma generates, and the trace sees it only through the scalar \mu = a\,z + b. That collapse is not unconditional. It rests on Markov stabilisation, which enters here as a hypothesis standing in for Jones' theorem rather than as something proved in place.

The proposition settles when that hypothesis may be invoked. Taking the word to be \sigma itself — the interface generator occurring a second time — the Hecke quadratic evaluates the left-hand side outright, and stabilisation collapses into a condition on z alone. The Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) misses it, and misses it by a quantity whose closed form factors into two positive-definite quadratics, q^2 \pm q + 1 = (q \pm \tfrac12)^2 + \tfrac34. The defect is therefore strictly negative at every q, not merely at the substrate value; no choice of pin recovers the identity.

The consequence is a condition on the braid word rather than on the algebra. The interface scalar \mu is available exactly when the interface generator appears once. Every canonical light-nucleus word satisfies this — the deuteron and tritium use their interface generator at index 2, helium-3 and helium-4 at index 5, one occurrence each — so the collapse holds where the framework applies it. What the proposition excludes is the assumption that it would keep holding on a word built to reuse that generator.

Scope. This is a structural exclusion, and the invariant is the closed form above rather than a numerical near-miss. It constrains the shape of the word, not the choice of interface element: an element a\,\sigma + b\,\mathbf{1} remains free, and nothing here bears on which one a derivation should select.
prop:binding-functional-is-the-log:
Proposition Only the logarithmic binding functional is extensive; the linear rival fails by -\alpha(1-x)(1-y) and carries a ceiling. Write t for a trace ratio and \alpha > 0 for the energy scale. The logarithmic functional B = -\alpha \ln t is extensive,

  -\alpha \ln(xy) \;=\; -\alpha \ln x \;+\; -\alpha \ln y
  \qquad (x, y > 0),

while the linear functional B = \alpha(1 - t) fails extensivity by an exact amount,

  \alpha(1 - xy) - \bigl[\alpha(1-x) + \alpha(1-y)\bigr]
    \;=\; -\alpha\,(1-x)(1-y),

which vanishes only when x = 1 or y = 1. Separately, since the atom trace is positive, \alpha(t_{\mathrm{free}} - t_{\mathrm{atom}}) < \alpha\,t_{\mathrm{free}}.

The Markov trace is multiplicative over independent subsystems, so an atom's trace factors as t_{\mathrm{atom}} = t_{\mathrm{free}} \prod_k \mu_k over its bonds. Energy, on the other hand, is extensive. A map carrying the first structure to the second must send products to sums — Cauchy's equation on (\mathbb{R}_{>0}, \times) — whose continuous solutions are the multiples of \ln.

The proposition records the part of that argument which is mechanically checkable: of the two functionals the framework has weighed, the logarithmic one is extensive and the linear one is not. The failure is stated as an identity rather than as a measurement, so it holds at every q and needs no anchor; a bond with x = 1 contributes nothing, so on any bond that binds at all the linear form is non-extensive.

The ceiling is an independent objection and does not rely on extensivity at all. With t_{\mathrm{free}} \approx 1 across the light nuclei, the linear form cannot produce a binding energy above \alpha \approx 4.19\ \mathrm{MeV}, which already excludes {}^{3}\mathrm{H}, {}^{4}\mathrm{He} and {}^{7}\mathrm{Li} against their measured values. Two separate reasons therefore point the same way.

Scope. The uniqueness step — that Cauchy's equation admits no continuous solutions beyond c \ln x — is classical and is not proved here, so the stronger reading, that the logarithmic form is forced rather than merely preferred among the two candidates, rests on it. What is proved is the comparison. Nothing here bears on the value of \alpha, which is fixed elsewhere, nor on whether the trace ratio entering the formula is the right one.
def:nucleon-pair-isospin-channel:
Definition Colour-system selection by isospin: \mathrm{select}(p) = \mathrm{altT_1} iff T(p) = 1. The colour side of the two-nucleon interface is settled by the isotypic decomposition: an ordered pair of colour sheets carries T_1 \otimes T_1 = A \oplus T_1 \oplus H, graded by exchange as \mathrm{Sym}^2 = A \oplus H of dimension 6 and \mathrm{Alt}^2 = T_1 of dimension 3. What that decomposition leaves open is which summand a given pair of nucleons draws on. Flavour supplies the answer, because flavour is a representation too.

A nucleon pair is one of the four channels

  p \;\in\; \{\, pp,\; nn,\; pn_{\mathrm{sym}},\; pn_{\mathrm{alt}} \,\},

carrying total isospin T(pp) = T(nn) = T(pn_{\mathrm{sym}}) = 1 and T(pn_{\mathrm{alt}}) = 0, the decomposition I = \tfrac12 \otimes I = \tfrac12 \;=\; (I{=}1) \oplus (I{=}0) of dimensions 3 + 1 = 2 \times 2. The colour system of a pair is the summand of T_1 \otimes T_1 its interface draws on, one of \mathrm{altT_1} = T_1 or \mathrm{symAH} = A \oplus H. The selection map is

  \mathrm{select}(p) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    \mathrm{altT_1}, & T(p) = 1, \\[2pt]
    \mathrm{symAH},  & T(p) = 0 .
  \end{cases}
rem:isospin-selection-class-inhabited:
Remark \mathrm{InterfaceExchangeAntisymmetry} is inhabited by \langle\mathrm{select},\,\mathrm{rfl}\rangle --- the class carries physics, not a constraint. The selection rule is carried by a conjecture class with two fields: a coupling assigning a colour system to each nucleon-pair channel, and the constraint that the coupling equals \mathrm{select}. Stated that way the class is inhabited by construction. Taking the coupling to be \mathrm{select} itself and the constraint to be reflexivity exhibits a witness, so the class constrains nothing as a mathematical object.

The opposite was previously asserted. A class whose only field is pinned to a definition already in scope cannot fail to be satisfiable, and an argument that leaned on its non-vacuity would be leaning on nothing.
prop:branching-identity-isospin-weights:
Proposition \mu_+ = y_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)}, \mu_- = y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)} --- hence at z = q^3/(q^2+1) the singlet draws nothing from the radical. Let \mathrm{tr}_M be any Markov trace on H_3(q), expanded in the Wedderburn basis as y_{(3)}\chi^{(3)} + y_{(2,1)}\chi^{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)}\chi^{(1^3)} and normalised by \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) = z. Then the two isospin scalars are sums over the H_2(q) \subset H_3(q) branching,

  \mu_+ \;=\; y_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)},
  \qquad
  \mu_- \;=\; y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)},

identically in z and in q. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), where y_{(1^3)} = 0, the singlet weight is therefore \mu_- = y_{(2,1)} exactly.
prop:interface-band-between-isospin-weig:
Proposition The admissible interface band [z-h,\,z] lies strictly between \mu_- and \mu_+. Let \mu = z + d with d \in [-h,\,0] be an admissible interface scalar, so that \mu ranges over the band [z-h,\,z]. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), whenever the two reduced inequalities

  q - z \;<\; (z-h)\,(q+q^{-1}),
  \qquad
  z\,(q+q^{-1}) \;<\; z + q^{-1}

hold, every admissible \mu satisfies

  \boxed{\;\; \mu_- \;<\; \mu \;<\; \mu_+ . \;\;}
cor:interface-never-realises-isospin-wei:
Corollary No admissible interface element realises either isospin weight: the two mechanisms compute on disjoint sets. Under the hypotheses of the band separation, every admissible interface scalar \mu = z + d with d \in [-h,\,0] satisfies

  \mu \;\ne\; \mu_-
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \mu \;\ne\; \mu_+ .

Strict inequalities on both sides give the two non-equalities directly. Stated this way the result is the sharpest form of the obstruction: it is not that the interface reproduces an isospin weight badly, it is that the interface never reproduces one at all.
rem:colour-tube-floor-overshoots-deutero: Remark The colour-tube selection rule cannot supply the interface tilt: a category error, corroborated by a family floor above the deuteron. The colour-tube channel weight is a natural candidate for the interface tilt d: it already assigns a rational weight to each pair of colour sheets, it is normalised, and it is upstream of the same D_6 structure the interface sits in. It cannot supply the tilt, and the reason is a category error rather than a numerical miss.
conj:spin-from-so3-fiber:
Conjecture Spin \mathrm{SU}(2)_S from full \mathrm{SO}(3) fiber action on color-sheet rotations. Conditional on the S_5 \leftrightarrow \mathrm{SO}(3) fiber action. Within the QOU framework, spin \mathrm{SU}(2)_S arises as the continuous lift of the full \mathrm{SO}(3) rotation group acting on the 3 color sheets per nucleon. This operates via the S_5 \to A_5 \cong I \subset \mathrm{SO}(3) icosahedral embedding on Bring's quintic surface. Extending to the full continuous \mathrm{SO}(3) populates the \ell = 2, 3, 4, \ldots spherical-harmonic decompositions. These contribute the h^4, h^6, \ldots corrections to the Borromean linking weight, which the current S_3-truncated framework omits.

The Family A linking weight (3q^2 + 4 + 3q^{-2})/4 = 5/2 + (3/4)h^2 terminates at h^2. The Borromean Markov trace's exact closed form has h^2 = 0 and first non-trivial coefficient h^4 = -3/4. The gap between Family A's (3/4)h^2 contribution and the Markov-trace h^4 = -3/4 structural value constitutes the load-bearing h^4 closure gap.

Spherical-harmonic levels of \mathrm{SO}(3) organise higher-order corrections. The icosahedral construction lives on A_5 \subset S_5, whereas the h^4 = -3/4 coefficient lives on the H_3 Borromean Markov trace. The missing object is a functor from the S_5/\mathrm{SO}(3) level \ell to a Wedderburn coefficient of the 3-strand H_3 trace.

Closing spin together with isospin unlocks Wigner \mathrm{SU}(4), the categorical source for nuclear-shell structure.
conj:wigner-su4-from-spin-isospin:
Conjecture Wigner \mathrm{SU}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)_S \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_I as the categorical source for nuclear-shell binding. Conditional on spin and isospin. The Wigner spin-isospin symmetry \mathrm{SU}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)_S \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_I arises in the QOU framework as the combined classical limit of the spin \mathrm{SO}(3) fiber action and the canonical isospin \mathbb{Z}/2 swap acting on the color-sheet flavor triples of nucleon braids. The A = 4 first magic shell (^{4}\!\mathrm{He}) forms the first \mathrm{SU}(4) supermultiplet (the trivial \mathbf{1} representation). This provides the categorical origin for the framework's "magic A\cdot 8G" closure.

The combined symmetry \mathrm{SU}(2)_S \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_I = \mathrm{SU}(4) acts on the four-dimensional internal space of each nucleon. The totally-antisymmetric tensor product of four nucleons fills the trivial representation \mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{SU}(4)}. This yields Wigner's 1937 supermultiplet theory. It explains the special status of ^{4}\!\mathrm{He} as a closed s-shell.

The framework's nuclear-shell binding relies on a hard-coded magic A·8G rule for ^{4}\!\mathrm{He} and an \alpha-cluster recursion for A \geq 8. This conjecture identifies the magic A\cdot 8G closure as the \mathrm{SU}(4) supermultiplet structure. The magic A\cdot 8G constant equals the \mathrm{SU}(4)-singlet projection coefficient of the saturated four-nucleon braid evaluated under the \mathrm{SO}(3)-fiber and bar-symmetric crystal functional.
rem:alpha-wigner-supermultiplet-context:
Remark The A=4 closure in the nuclear-physics literature: the Wigner \mathrm{SU}(4) supermultiplet. The A=4 magic shell is the first Wigner \mathrm{SU}(4) supermultiplet. The four single-nucleon spin-isospin states span the fundamental of \mathrm{SU}(4). Their totally antisymmetric product forms the one-dimensional singlet \Lambda^{4}(\mathbb{C}^{4}): the closed shell of {}^{4}\mathrm{He}. The vanishing dimension \dim \Lambda^{A}(\mathbb{C}^{4}) = 0 for A > 4 fixes the A = 4 locality of the closure.

Standard nuclear-mass systematics treat this closed-shell binding phenomenologically. The Wigner mass term vanishes identically at N = Z. It does not account for the anomalous extra binding of the even-even self-conjugate nuclei. A separate empirical cusp correction supplies that binding.

This binding is located directly in the representation content of the nucleon braids. The T = 0 isoscalar channel — the self-conjugate partition (2,2) \vdash 4 — reproduces this scale with zero free parameters. The fully antisymmetric \Lambda^{4} channel acts as the closed-shell supermultiplet. The binding that nuclear phenomenology supplies through the Wigner term is here fixed by the \mathrm{SU}(4) structure of the A = 4 shell.
conj:weinberg-angle-categorical:
Conjecture Weinberg angle \theta_W as Hecke-eigenvalue ratio on the EW Hoefsmit projectors. Let R be the categorical coefficient ring with generic q \in R. Under the Hoefsmit cell-content identification of the EW triplet inside \mathrm{End}_R(V^{\otimes 6}), W \leftrightarrow \sigma_1^4, Z \leftrightarrow \sigma_3^6, H \leftrightarrow \sigma_5^8. The Standard Model Weinberg angle \theta_W is the categorical scalar in R given by

  \cos\theta_W
  \;:=\;
  \frac{\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(e_W^{+} \cdot \sigma_1^4\bigr)}
       {\sqrt{\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(e_W^{+} \cdot \sigma_1^4\bigr)^2
              + \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(e_B^{+} \cdot \sigma_5^8\bigr)^2}},
  \sin\theta_W
  \;:=\;
  \frac{\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(e_B^{+} \cdot \sigma_5^8\bigr)}
       {\sqrt{\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(e_W^{+} \cdot \sigma_1^4\bigr)^2
              + \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(e_B^{+} \cdot \sigma_5^8\bigr)^2}},

where e_W^{+}, e_B^{+} are the Hoefsmit-projector idempotents on the symmetric channels of the W and B slots respectively. The B slot is understood pre-EWSB before W^3/B mixing.

At n = 6, the Hoefsmit identification assigns \sigma_1^4 to W, \sigma_3^6 to Z, and \sigma_5^8 to H. Pre-EWSB, the Hoefsmit slot \sigma_5^8 corresponds to the pre-mixing B generator. The rotation by \theta_W sends (W^3, B) \mapsto (Z, \gamma). This rotation acts as a specific change-of-basis in the Hoefsmit projector decomposition.

Evaluating \mathrm{tr}_M(e_W^{+} \cdot \sigma_1^4) / \mathrm{tr}_M(e_B^{+} \cdot \sigma_5^8) at the pure pattern yields \cot\theta_W \stackrel{?}{=} q^{-4} \approx 0.6588. This fails to match the 1.823 CODATA target. A correct categorical derivation must apply the non-uniform pure-pattern multiplicities, incorporate the categorical-linking operation, and potentially weight the trace by the Higgs vacuum expectation value. Each of these repairs acts inside the carrier, which is where a repair must act: \mathrm{tr}_M decomposes as \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda and the Schur–Weyl row cap sets y_\lambda = 0 for every \ell(\lambda) > N, so at the fibre dimension N = 2 the definition above is blind to the blocks with three or more rows by construction. A construction that reaches the CODATA value by reading the spectrum of such a block instead is not a competing evaluation of \cos\theta_W as defined here; it is a reading of a module the carrier does not contain. Expressing \theta_W as a ratio of categorical scalars remains structurally consistent. Proving this conjecture supplies \sin\theta_W, \cos\theta_W \in R as categorical scalars, closing the Weinberg-angle gap.

This conjecture gates the Coulomb term. Neither the braid nor any invariant pair coupling produces a Coulomb pair term between nucleon blocks (the Coulomb-charge definition). The invariant coupling with the right Cartan shape is the unbroken neutral exchange g^2\,T_3T_3' + g'^2\,(Y/2)(Y'/2), and it splits identically as e^2\,QQ' + g_Z^2\,(T_3 - s^2Q)(T_3' - s^2Q') with Q = T_3 + Y/2, s^2 = g'^2/(g^2+g'^2) and e^2 = g^2 s^2 (the flavour-charge remark). Here \tan\theta_W = g'/g, so s^2 = \sin^2\theta_W is exactly the scalar this conjecture would supply, and e^2 \neq 0 requires \sin\theta_W \neq 0. The conjecture is necessary for the Coulomb term but not sufficient. On nucleon blocks the exchange with a fraction \lambda of the second term kept has the Coulomb form if and only if \lambda = 0, whatever the value of s^2, so a mass scale for the Z that removes the second term at nuclear distance is a separate input; no such scale is derived in this framework. Until both are supplied, the Coulomb energy used in the binding Lagrangian is an import.
sec:nuclear-binding-intro: Once the two-nucleon isospin channel is selected, extending the linear-programming deficit profile across the (Z, N) lattice determines the global stability landscape of composite nuclei. This section defines the LP demand profile and demand stability criterion, proves that the nuclear binding operator partitions the (Z, N) chart into three distinct structural regimes—the torus-knot regime for light nuclei, the Hopf-link regime across intermediate shells, and the post-magic regime above closed shells—and formulates the periodic-table demand conjecture linking deficit minima to the empirical magic numbers.
